text: In the coming decades, artificial intelligence is expected to evolve far beyond today's specialized tools. Researchers predict we will eventually achieve Artificial General Intelligence, or AGI, which means machines that can think, learn, and reason across any task just like a human. However, experts disagree on the timeline—some believe AGI could arrive within 25 years, while others think it may take a century. The potential benefits are enormous, from personalized medicine and solving climate change to automating tedious work. Yet, there are serious risks: job displacement, privacy loss, and even the danger of AI acting contrary to human values. Therefore, developing strong ethical safeguards will be critical as this technology advances.
